comment: Release conditions for every exact-pinned version in package.json (dependencies, devDependencies and overrides),
plus any override added to clear an npm audit advisory. An exact pin is invisible to update-npm-deps.ps1 - that
script upgrades caret ranges and skips exact versions - so nothing would ever remind you a pin is stale. This file
is what makes that check happen: on every run the script executes each `check` and compares its trimmed stdout to
`expect`. Equal means the pin is still required; different means the condition that justified the pin has changed
and the pin should be re-examined. `check: null` means no mechanical test exists - it is reported for manual review
on every run instead of going quiet. Every exact pin must have an entry here, and every entry must name a package
that is actually present in the declared section; the script reports either mismatch. See rule G100.

@codemirror/language.why: Must match the copy Obsidian bundles at runtime: Obsidian registers '@codemirror/language' in the module map it hands to plugins, so this copy is types-only and a newer pin would declare API the runtime lacks. Unlike @codemirror/state and @codemirror/view it is NOT named in obsidian's peerDependencies, so npm cannot detect or correct a mismatch. Settled 2026-08-05 by marker comparison: Obsidian carried 6.11.2 through 1.13.0 and bundles 6.12.3 from 1.13.1 onward, so 6.12.3 is what BOTH the latest public (1.13.4) and the latest catalyst (1.13.5) run.
@codemirror/language.manualCheck: No mechanical check exists here: it would have to read a sibling obsidian-versions checkout, which this repo does not own (G37). Re-derive by marker comparison against the target version's obsidian.asar/app.js. The bundle embeds no version string, and Obsidian ships a PATCHED copy - it exports four names no published release has (ignoreSpellcheckToken, lineClassNodeProp, lineHighlighter, tokenClassNodeProp) - so an export-list comparison can never match a release exactly and only code markers can date it. Grep app.js for these, each introduced by a known release: 'maxBufferLength: 512' (6.11.3, was 2048), 'EnterBracketed' (6.12.1), '.paused' in the bracket-matching ViewPlugin (6.12.2), 'doc.length) return null' in matchBrackets (6.12.3), 'rangesToFold' in the fold state field (6.12.4). The newest marker present and the oldest marker absent bracket the version. Then run build:compile plus the editor-extension tests. Verified 2026-08-05 against 1.13.4 and 1.13.5: both 6.12.3.

@codemirror/state.why: obsidian's peerDependencies names this exact version. A second copy in the tree means two CodeMirror state instances at runtime, so editor extensions would attach to the wrong one.

@codemirror/view.why: Same as @codemirror/state - obsidian peer-pins it exactly, and the view layer must run against Obsidian's own CodeMirror instance.

@puppeteer/browsers.why: Clears GHSA-jmr9-qjv8-65gv (extract-zip unvalidated symlink path traversal, 8 high advisories) and nothing else. extract-zip is vulnerable at every published version, so there is no patched version to override it to, and the direct dependency cannot be bumped either: obsidian-integration-testing is already latest and pins webdriverio, and even the newest webdriverio still reaches extract-zip through @wdio/utils -> @puppeteer/browsers ^2.x. @puppeteer/browsers@3 replaced extract-zip with modern-tar, so forcing 3.x on @wdio/utils - the only consumer left on 2.x - removes the subtree entirely. It also dedupes: puppeteer-core already brings 3.2.0 into this tree, so the override collapses two copies into one rather than adding anything. The major bump is safe because @wdio/utils imports only install, canDownload, resolveBuildId, detectBrowserPlatform, Browser, ChromeReleaseChannel, computeExecutablePath and the InstallOptions type, all still exported by 3.x with compatible signatures, and both packages are ESM-only. NEVER take the `npm audit fix --force` remedy here: it downgrades obsidian-integration-testing from 10.x to 1.1.2 (rule G100). Mirrors the same override in obsidian-dev-utils.
@puppeteer/browsers.manualCheck: The check reads @wdio/utils's own declared range, not a version, because that range is what makes the override necessary. When it moves to ^3 or later, @wdio/utils no longer pulls extract-zip on its own and this override can be deleted along with this entry. A `require('@wdio/utils/package.json')` check would not work - its exports map does not expose package.json - hence the readFileSync form, which resolves relative to the package root the sweep runs from.

brace-expansion.why: GHSA-mh99-v99m-4gvg (high, DoS via unbounded expansion) is declared with the single flat range <=5.0.7, which in plain semver also matches the newest 1.x and 2.x releases - so no release on those lines can ever satisfy it and `npm audit fix` can only offer a downgrade. Every copy must therefore be forced onto >=5.0.8. A bare caret override cannot do that: 5.x exports a namespace (exports.expand), while minimatch 3/5 require the module itself and minimatch 8/9 default-import it, so they break with `expand is not a function`. The override points at patches/brace-expansion-callable, a wrapper re-exporting the patched 5.x implementation in BOTH shapes (callable default, and named .expand for minimatch 10). The patched implementation installs under the brace-expansion-upstream alias because the override takes over the real name.
brace-expansion.manualCheck: The check tests the condition that makes the wrapper necessary: the patched upstream exporting a namespace rather than a callable. `object` means old consumers still need the wrapper; `function` would mean upstream restored a callable default and the wrapper can go. The wrapper is also unnecessary once no tree copy of minimatch below 10 remains - verify by grepping node_modules/**/minimatch for `require("brace-expansion")` and `__importDefault` before dropping it.

deepmerge-ts.why: Clears GHSA-ggr8-5vv4-36mx (deepmerge-ts stack exhaustion when merging recursive object graphs), patched in 8.0.0. Reached only transitively, through webdriverio -> @wdio/config / @wdio/utils / webdriver, and no direct bump gets there: every wdio package still declares deepmerge-ts@^7.0.3, the newest release included. NEVER take the `npm audit fix --force` remedy: it downgrades obsidian-integration-testing from 10.x to 1.1.2 (rule G100). The forced major is safe for these consumers. 8.0.0 breaks by renaming the mergeInfo system and aligning the customization shorthand, and a scan of the whole installed tree found only two bindings in use, `deepmerge` and `deepmergeCustom`. Both `deepmergeCustom` shapes present were run against 7.1.6 and 8.0.1 and produce identical output: @wdio/config's `mergeArrays` handler, which reads `meta.key` and returns `utils.actions.defaultMerge`, and webdriver's `deepmergeCustom({ mergeArrays: false })`. Mirrors the same override in obsidian-dev-utils.
deepmerge-ts.manualCheck: The check reads the range @wdio/utils declares, not a version, because that range is what forces the override. When it moves to ^8 or later the override and this entry can both go. Before lifting it, re-run the deepmergeCustom probe rather than trusting the range alone: @wdio/config passes a handler that reads `meta.key`, and that is precisely the API 8.0.0 renamed, so a regression there would be silent rather than a crash.

typescript.why: TypeScript 7 (tsgo) breaks this toolchain: @typescript-eslint's parser crashes on the native API, so type-aware ESLint cannot run on 7. @typescript-eslint peer-requires the range below, so 6.x is the last usable major. Hold until obsidian-dev-utils migrates.
